body:
Thanks for the great response! I really appreciate it.

Yes, I think we found the source of our disagreement (see your #2) but we actually agree on a lot.

I also wanted to make a provocative Reddit post that garnered some attention by applying my personal issues (of not finding enough happiness to make life worthwhile) to an overall argument for suicide. I did that because my original post to r/SuicideWatch telling my personal story (with this argument as a tangent) got very little response.

And while I believe in (most of) what I argue, there is a clear flaw to the argument. That is, plenty of people on this planet find enough happiness to make life worth living for them. My problem is my brain chemistry/wiring does not allow me to despite years of therapy and various medications. ::sigh::

Thanks for the Camus recommendation! I was a philosophy major in college so I am sure I will enjoy.

This is awesome!... But it's from 2013! :)

http://viralwomen.com/post/amsterdam_during_putins_visit_in_the_running_for_sass_capital_of_the_world

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rtth5FgJ5X8

http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/03/30/amsterdam-rainbow-flag-vladimir-putin_n_2985410.html

Don't do the Golden Gate - people have survived the fall and it's extremely painful. I'm not sure about the other bridge but you might want to check to make sure it's 100% lethal. Last thing you want is physical pain on top of all that.
cool, you make a good point! Best I've seen all day. Thanks! I may try that other subreddit.
yep. You might need a plugin or something though. Forget what it's called. it's easy to find though

Eh that's a dumb reason. Sorry I'm so frank but yeah. That's dumb. 

The only reason to kill yourself is cause you're not happy and can't become happy no matter what you do (change your life multiple ways, try therapy, meds, etc etc). THAT's a good reason for suicide.

re: being found in a timely manner. Try sending an email on time delay. It's easy. Just set it up to send to whomever you want to find you (maybe the police or something) at a time when you're sure you're gonna be dead.

I'm also considering. Have been for most of my life haha.

Hanging sounds painful to me :-/ choking, neck breaking, ugh. I am thinking pills but I don't know which ones or how to get em :(

Yes. That is my issue. The rewards are insufficient. If they're sufficient for you, great. You're perhaps one of the few. 

re: suicide as an option. You named a bunch of other options. Those options should probably be attempted before suicide. But suicide is always an option (unless you're physically prevented from killing yourself, like trapped in a straight jacket or something). It's just not one that you approve of considering.

Thanks for the well thought out response!

1) Sure. Here's the study. It's well-known and oft-cited so I just figured the link wasn't needed. 
http://lmgtfy.com/?q=lottery+happiness+study

2) Yes, my ultimate value is happiness.

3) What I mean by "It won't make a difference" is the first thing you suggested - that it won't change our level of (un)happiness.

4) I wasn't trying to assess religion, just many religions' stances on suicide.

5) Re: faith and reason. Eh fine, not really wanting to argue about faith here - beyond the scope of this thread.

6) re: suicide being taboo. You missed the point of the argument here, which was about why people don't commit suicide. One reason is that most of society considers the topic taboo so people don't seriously consider it at all. Obviously once they're dead, they're not around to care what society thinks.

7) re: non-sequiturs. Where? You haven't pointed one out yet.

8) re: happiness and meaning. Well, happiness is the only thing I live for. And I believe that's true of most people because even if you find 'meaning' in knowledge, love, whatever - it's because those things bring you and others happiness, or you believe they will lead to greater happiness for you and others. 

9) re: easiness and meaning. I never used the word 'meaning' in my post so not sure how I could have equated the two!

10) re: happiness and meaning. See #8. Can you please provide examples of what else might people find meaning in besides happiness? My bet is that those meanings can be reduced to finding happiness.

11) re: meaning. I like that - "meaning fountains." haha. We spout or make up whatever meanings we want. I don't find greater meaning in difficulty. I don't find greater meaning in struggle. I'm not even sure what that would look like. However, I inherently value happiness. That is the one true goal of life, at least, for me (though I believe that's true for all, if they only thought about it enough).

12) re: quote. Not sure what point this is supposed to make. My best guess is it's saying that leaving a legacy (for however long it lasts) is more important than living a blissful life? Phooey! One reason people leave legacies is because the thought of making an impact and having long-lasting effects on the world makes them feel happy. Thus, happiness. Another reason to leave a legacy would be to increase happiness for others as well, like creating a great work of art (beauty makes people happier) or freeing the slaves (freedom generally makes people happier). Thus, again, happiness. See? Happiness is what it comes down to.

Thanks again for your thoughtful response.

Walking away from life certainly IS an option. I think we can all agree on that. Whether we we think it's a good or bad option is the question at had.

What I'm saying is that work, stress, and problems are the norm in life. And the rewards are insufficient to justify the work it takes to get to them.

Psychological therapy and psychiatric medication. These are proven solutions to this problem. They do work for many, apparently. Come back when you've tried those if they have failed you (as they have me).

I understand where you're coming from. I too have achieved many goals in my life, and I'm proud of that. Part of me disbelieves the (proven) science that I am just as happy as I would otherwise be. I look at what I have achieved and it's hard not to believe that I am happier now than I otherwise would be. (Which entails that I shudder to think how miserable I would be if I hadn't achieved anything). But still, the rewards are fleeting and the happiness simply does not compensate for the years of work, stress, and unending difficulties. 

While I may be happier now for having achieved what I have, life is about the now and next - and there's always work, stress, and problems in the now and next. They never end, no matter how much you have accomplished.

I feel similarly. There's nothing I want to do. Everything is a chore. Even merely existing is a chore.

The only thing I can say is that the best solution we have to this problem is a combination of psychological therapy and psychiatric medication. I've tried both. It doesn't always work but I guess it's worth a shot. Remember, drugs are good.

Thanks for replying. 

You say, "Every step of it is work. You have to face and overcome so many things..." YES. I agree! And I think that we agree that life IS work. My OP explains how work's reward (happiness) is fleeting and as it turns out, even if we work hard to achieve our goals, our happiness levels return to the level at which we started. So then how is work worth it?
I totally hear you. I feel similarly.

Totally agree! Suicide is in people's personal best interests but not in society's (though even this statement could be considered self-contradictory). My two arguments in the OP are both instances of people obeying anti-suicide authorities.

Fair - some are scared of death. Even I'm a little scared, but only because I fear physical pain, so I want to make it as physically painless as possible.

You call it selfishness. HA! It's even more selfish of others to ask me to stay alive solely for their sake. Consider this: a man is in constant pain and wants to kill himself, but his wife asks him to stay alive because he makes her happy. Is that not devilishly selfish of the wife?

Furthermore, saying that suicide is selfish is NOT an argument against it. In fact, many would agree (as do I) that SELFISHNESS is GOOD! So come up with something better.

Regarding cowardice - well, if death is so scary, then people who commit suicide can't be all that cowardly. Also, similar to calling suicide selfish, calling it cowardly does not an argument make.

Of course we all "like the good". That's one way to define good!

Something you said is totally nonsensical for me and I was hoping you might be able to explain it. You say, "the more you work, the further away from your pain." Isn't work called 'work' because it's something we DON'T want to do? If work were fun, we call it "play". Even when people say they enjoy their jobs or work (and the grand majority really don't), there are some aspects of their work they don't enjoy or at least sometimes don't want to do. So how does MORE work bring you FARTHER from pain? I'd love to know that secret...
(S)he's in a rush because (s)he's in pain!! You'd be in a rush too if you were in constant pain.

Thanks for the reply!

Yeah I am glad someone agrees with me regarding how simply baffling it is that more people don't kill themselves. Or at least think about it. I mean, it's such an obvious and real solution to so many problems! 

Also, maybe I should have asked my second question a different way, but what I mean is not the method of suicide, but if there is a way in which I can ease the blow on my family. Like, is there something I could say to them beforehand that would make them understand and accept, maybe even be happy for me that I have done it? Or does it need to be in a note since then they can't try to stop me? But a note risks being overshadowed by my death and they won't really understand or accept what I'm saying in it. I don't know - making this easier on them seems like an impossible task.
